mentl/49ed405:
The 6.3 modal sweep's next rule found a leak rather than a crucible.
`handler hf with s = op() { g() => resume(s) }` installed by
`fn bad() with !E = (g()) ~> hf` checks CLEAN, and T_OverDeclared volunteers
that the body "only uses Pure".

The init really performs, which is what makes it a leak and not a dead
expression: give op a handler returning 7, install both as
`((g()) ~> hf) ~> he`, and the program exits 7 — the value reached s through
an install-time performance of E resolved by the outer handler.

The control refuses, so the position is the variable: the identical `op()` in
bad()'s body is `E_EffectMismatch: !E + Any vs E`. And arms already charge —
tests/crown/leak-arm-adds-row refuses on the same shape one layer over — so
this is not "the tee never adds", it is the init sitting off whatever channel
the arms ride.

The handler's type has nowhere to put it. `mentl query "type hf"` projects
Handler(F): the effect handled, with no row for what the handler performs.
SYNTAX's tee rule is row(expr ~> h) = row(expr) - handled(h) + row(h), and
the + row(h) half has no carrier in that type. infer.mn's PTee comment says
so in as many words — "we don't have handler-value typing so arm_row can't be
extracted from RHS" — a comment measured true this turn, pointing at the same
hole.

Stamped as Hbeta.effects.handler-state-init-row-never-installed. Traced:
infer_handler_state_inits walks each init at handler-DECLARATION time, so the
row lands on the frame judging the decl rather than on any installer, while
at runtime the init evaluates once per install in the installer's world. The
honest reading is SYNTAX's own — an init is part of the handler, its row
belongs in row(h), and the tee already carries that to every installer. Not a
new concept and not a fork; the rule is written and the carrier is missing.

Writers NOT enumerated: where the arm row reaches an installer is the unfound
half and the build's first move, because that channel is the working
precedent this fix s

mentl/49f0165:
Pre-fix: $parse_variants only handled paren-fields `Bar(T1, T2)`. Wheel-
source uses record-field variants `Bar { w: List<Float>, x: List<Float> }`
heavily (lib/ml/autodiff.mn TapeEntry, src/types.mn record-shaped variant
ADTs). After parsing vname, the parser saw `{` (TLBrace), didn't match
TLParen, treated variant as nullary, and left `{ field: type, ... }`
tokens in the stream. Downstream parse_stmt consumed those tokens as
mangled top-level stmts → cascade of LUnresolved names (str_concat 512,
list_index 227, list_tail 177, list_head 172, list_set 114, make_list 98,
slice 60, byte_at 52 = 1232 of the top hits) for fns whose registrations
were lost in the cascade.

Post-fix: $parse_variants peeks TLBrace before TLParen. If TLBrace,
delegates to existing $parse_record_type_fields (already used by
nominal-record path at parse_type_stmt:28-52), wraps result in
mk_TyRecord, and stores as a 1-element field_tys list. Mirrors the
nominal-record pattern verbatim — same downstream variant-tuple shape
(name, [TyRecord(fields)]), same lower/emit consumption.

Empirical:
  Pre-fix:  full wheel → 2902 UNRESOLVED, 0 wat2wasm errors.
  Post-fix: full wheel →  448 UNRESOLVED (85% reduction).
            Top names changed from runtime helpers (str_concat 512, etc.)
            to type-projection terms (handle 160, reason 16, origin 12).
  Side: 11 wat2wasm errors surfaced. NOT new bugs — pre-existing handler-
  with-state-init emit gaps that the unresolved `(unreachable)` from
  `UNRESOLVED: map` was masking. With map now resolved (because its
  registration is no longer lost in the autodiff parser cascade), the
  emitted (call_indirect) enforces strict stack discipline → the LFloat
  0.0 placeholder pushed by `with state = 0.0` clause leaks an i32 onto
  stack. Named follow-up Hβ.emit.handler-with-state-init-consumes —
  the emit's handler-with-state mechanism must store the INIT value
  into the handler-state record, not leave it on stack. Surfaced bug,
  not regression.
